title: U.S. House · Illinois's 8th District
area: Northwest Chicago suburbs in Cook County, including Schaumburg, Hoffman Estates, Elk Grove Village and Palatine.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Raja Krishnamoorthi is running for U.S. Senate rather than seeking re-election here. Melissa Bean, who represented this district in Congress from 2005 to 2011, won a seven-way March 17, 2026 Democratic primary. Jennifer Davis won the Republican primary. Ballotpedia calculated the district's Cook Partisan Voter Index as D+5, based on the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections.

summary.text: Melissa Bean is the Democratic nominee for the open Illinois 8th District seat, which she previously represented in Congress from 2005 to 2011. She has since worked in business, including at JPMorgan Chase and Mesirow Financial, and won the March 2026 Democratic primary.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Maine East High School and a bachelor's degree from Roosevelt University.
Career experience includes owning a business and serving as U.S. Representative for Illinois's 8th District from 2005 to 2011.
Has been affiliated with One Million Degrees, Junior Achievement, World Business Chicago, JPMorgan Chase and Mesirow Financial.
As a member of Congress, voted for the Affordable Care Act, TARP, the 2009 stimulus bill, the auto industry bailout, the 'Cash for Clunkers' program, and cap-and-trade climate legislation.

priorities.text: Says she would protect and strengthen the Affordable Care Act, including protections for pre-existing conditions, and allow Medicare to negotiate prescription drug prices directly.

Says masked ICE agents have been deployed unnecessarily into communities and calls for DHS Secretary Kristi Noem's firing or removal, greater ICE oversight including body cameras, and accountability for agents who exceed their authority.
Says she would codify Roe v. Wade protections, expand healthcare privacy protections, and oppose any federal abortion ban.

positions.summary: Voted for the Affordable Care Act while in Congress and says she would protect and strengthen it, including allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices.
Says she would work to codify Roe v. Wade protections and oppose any federal abortion ban.
Calls for greater ICE oversight and accountability, and opposes what she describes as unnecessary deployment of masked ICE agents into communities.
Says she has a record of supporting science-based climate policy and will work to cut emissions and scale clean energy.
Campaign platform emphasizes closing wealth gaps through worker profit-sharing and pension incentives, without a direct statement on raising taxes on high earners or corporations.

record.text: As a member of Congress in 2009-2010, voted with the House Democratic leadership 90.8% of the time according to a July 2010 analysis, and voted for TARP, the 2009 stimulus bill, the auto bailout, 'Cash for Clunkers,' cap-and-trade, and the Affordable Care Act.

summary.text: Jennifer Davis is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 8th District, an entrepreneur who co-founded the software company Davisware and won the March 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Co-founded Davisware, a service-technology software company, with her husband at age 17, and later launched BExponential, a business focused on helping women.
Wrote a book, "Living Exponentially in Life and Business."

priorities.text: Says affordability is the top issue in the district and pledges to cut federal taxes on working families and ease regulations on small businesses.
Says she would champion policies to help small businesses, which she says employ 44% of Illinois's workforce, by cutting taxes and streamlining regulations.

Proposes a "Digital Dome" national cybersecurity shield to protect families and the military from cyberattacks and online predators, and supports expanding U.S. oil, gas and renewable energy production.

positions.summary: Pledges to cut federal taxes on working families and ease regulations on small businesses and entrepreneurs.
Says she would drive energy independence by expanding U.S. oil, gas and renewable production to cut reliance on other countries.
